title: Parallel Runtime Interface for Fortran (PRIF): A Multi-Image Solution for LLVM Flang
problem: Fortran compilers implementing parallel features have runtime libraries tightly coupled to specific compiler implementations and communication libraries, limiting portability and standardization across different systems.
motivation: Standardizing the interface between Fortran compilers and runtime libraries is essential for enabling widespread adoption of parallel Fortran across diverse HPC platforms and architectures.
method: PRIF defines a standardized set of Fortran procedures corresponding to each parallel feature in the Fortran standard, allowing any compiler to invoke these procedures and any runtime library to implement them. This decouples compiler-specific details from runtime library implementation. The design supports both shared-memory and distributed-memory systems while maintaining portability across different operating systems, toolchains, and architectures. Caffeine is provided as a prototype implementation.
key_novelty: A compiler-agnostic and runtime-library-agnostic standardized interface that enables flexible and portable parallel Fortran support across heterogeneous HPC systems.
contributions: PRIF: a generalized interface covering all Fortran standard parallel features
Compiler-independent and runtime-library-independent design for flexibility
Support for both shared-memory and distributed-memory systems
Caffeine prototype demonstrating portability across platforms and toolchains
limitations: Performance evaluation, scalability results, and comparison with existing Fortran parallel implementations are not discussed.
primary_theme: Standardized compiler-runtime interface for parallel Fortran
